raw_response:
I am old now, and I do not play with too many changes. On my 14 mu, I will still keep most land in the wheat-maize rotation because that is the steady way here, and I will keep a smaller piece in cotton so if one crop has a bad year, I still have another way to earn. I will put about 10 mu into wheat-maize and 4 mu into cotton. Wheat and maize feed into each other on the same land, and cotton gives me some cash, but cotton takes more watching and more hand work, so I will not plant too much because some people in my family work outside and labor is tight.

For wheat, I will manage it the old way, not too little and not too much. If I am too stingy on fertilizer, wheat turns yellow and yield falls, and that loss hurts more than spending a bit extra. But I also cannot pour in too much because fertilizer and pumping water both cost money. So I will do a base dressing, then another round around jointing, and irrigate when the crop really needs it. After wheat harvest I will put maize in quickly, because the turnaround is short and I do not have time for fancy tillage. Cotton I will keep on the lighter side of the farm. I will fertilize it, water it a couple of times from the well if the sky stays dry, and spray only when I really see insects or weeds getting ahead.
